description: The bar chart illustrates the performance of two fine-tuned models — NESAC ft model (orange) and SESHA ft model (green) — across five different text preprocessing optimisations applied to speech recognition data: “Normalised”, “Add Spacing”, “Remove Spacing”, “Americanisms”, and “Dates”. The horizontal axis represents the model output score (likely a loss or error metric, given the small decimal values), ranging from 0.000 to approximately 0.0035, with tick marks at 0.000, 0.001, 0.002, and 0.003. Each optimisation has two adjacent horizontal bars, with the NESAC model’s value labeled to the right of its bar and the SESHA model’s value similarly labeled. For “Normalised”, NESAC scores 0.00334 and SESHA 0.00323; for “Add Spacing”, NESAC is 0.00319 and SESHA 0.00344; for “Remove Spacing”, NESAC is 0.00311 and SESHA 0.00306; for “Americanisms”, NESAC is 0.00299 and SESHA 0.00302; and for “Dates”, NESAC is 0.00257 and SESHA 0.00228. The chart shows that SESHA generally outperforms NESAC on “Normalised”, “Remove Spacing”, and “Dates”, while NESAC performs better on “Add Spacing” and “Americanisms”. The bars are not sorted by value, and no bars are visually emphasized beyond color coding. The legend at the bottom clarifies the color mapping to each model. This chart likely supports the paper’s focus on adapting Whisper for regional dialects by evaluating how different text normalisation strategies affect model performance across two regional fine-tuned variants.
